key_insight: Combining clinical data with hospital workload indicators and end-to-end text fine-tuning improved ICU readmission risk prediction, while directly adding raw text embeddings hurt tree-model performance.
clinical_relevance: Operation-aware risk estimates could inform ICU discharge review, but clinical benefit and safety remain unproven.
method: Used multi-agent extraction and self-evolving retrieval-augmented generation to reduce template noise in progress notes.
Integrated notes, vital signs, ICD/DRG codes, admission flow, and departmental workload indicators.
Applied class reweighting, threshold calibration, and multimodal Transformer fine-tuning with layer-wise freezing and differential learning rates.
evidence_signal: Across 20 independent runs on 20,000 MIMIC-III ICU stays with approximately 10.5% readmissions, the best model achieved AUROC 0.8288 ± 0.0110, PR-AUC 0.4373 ± 0.0310, and F1 0.4757 ± 0.0196.
watch_item: The abstract reports no external or prospective validation; generalizability and effects on discharge safety and alarm burden need evaluation.
paper_title: Operation-aware Multimodal Clinical Decision Support System for ICU Discharge Risk Assessment
